title: Why China Gives Away Its Best AI Models
hook: Moonshot's Kimi K3 reportedly matches top US systems at a fraction of the cost — and you can just download it. Giving the model away isn't charity; it's strategy.
key_points: Chinese labs increasingly release 'open-weight' models: the trained model is free to download and run.
Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 reportedly beats some leading US systems at far lower cost.
Free, capable models undercut the subscription and API revenue US labs are counting on.
Wide adoption also makes a country's models the default global infrastructure — influence without export controls.
The Verge reports Silicon Valley spent the week on 'red alert' digesting the release.
content_html: There's an obvious question buried in the news that Chinese labs keep releasing world-class AI models for free: why would anyone give away something that cost a fortune to build? The Verge's answer is that it isn't generosity — it's one of the sharpest competitive moves available.
extra_html: An "open-weight" model is one whose trained parameters are published, so anyone can download it and run it themselves instead of renting access from a company. When a free model is good enough, the business model of the labs charging for access starts to wobble — and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, reportedly matching some of the best US systems at a fraction of the cost, is exactly that kind of pressure. The second payoff is subtler: models that everyone builds on become infrastructure, and infrastructure is influence you don't need export controls to project. The upside for the rest of us is real — cheaper, more private, more independent AI that doesn't require anyone's permission to run. The complication is that the same openness makes the technology impossible for anyone, including its makers, to recall.

related.hook: Two Chinese labs released frontier-rivaling models within days of each other — one now reportedly the largest open-weight model ever — at prices well below their US competitors.

related.title: China's Free-to-Download Models Are Closing the Gap
related.hook: A Chinese lab's openly downloadable model reportedly rivals the top US models at some security tasks — a sign the distance between open AI and the frontier is shrinking fast.

related.title: Who Controls AI?
related.hook: The most powerful AI models are built by a handful of giant companies, because training them costs a fortune. Who holds that power — and whether 'open' AI can balance it — shapes everything.

flashcards.prompt: Why would a lab give away a model it spent enormous sums to train?

choices.text: Free capable models undercut rivals' paid business and spread its technology as the default
Open-weight models are cheaper to train than closed ones
Regulators require all models to be free

flashcards.explanation_html: Releasing weights is competitive strategy: it erodes the subscription revenue closed labs depend on, while making your model the base others build on.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'open-weight' mean, in plain terms?
flashcards.back_html: The trained model itself is published, so anyone can download it and run it on their own machines — unlike closed models you can only rent through a company's service.

flashcards.prompt: What reportedly put Silicon Valley on 'red alert' this week?

A US ban on training new models
The shutdown of a major cloud provider
